results.summary: ZMINA:Resilience. Rolling call for International Showcasing of co-creation projects
results.content: ZMINA:Resilience. Rolling call for International Showcasing of co-creation projects

beneficiaryAdministration:
IZOLYATSIA Foundation (UA) and Malý Berlín (SK) together with Trans Europe Halles (SE) announce the rolling open call for cultural and arts organisations within the ZMINA:Resilience project, strand "Support for international showcasing of co-creation projects".

The objective of this call is to support projects that bring artistic and cultural works co-created by Ukrainian and other Creative Europe cultural organisations to wider audiences through public showcasing and presentation events in Ukraine and across other Creative Europe countries.

Funding will be provided to projects featuring co-creations made by partnerships involving at least one organisation from Ukraine and at least one organisation from another Creative Europe country. The projects should maximise the visibility, audience reach, sustainability, and future showcasing potential of these works.

Supported projects are expected to include active partner cooperation to adapt showcased works to new audiences, for example by contextualising works, providing translation, involving local artists, experts and communities, conducting parallel programmes, and similar approaches.

All creative and cultural sectors are eligible except audiovisual.

Project Objectives

  1. Showcase and tour co-creations that explore the theme of resilience in any arts or cultural sector except audiovisual.
  2. Hold a minimum of 6 public presentation events: at least 3 events in each of at least two countries, one of which must be Ukraine.
  3. The presentation events cannot take place in the home city or town of any of the applicant organisations.

Overall Strand Budget

Total funding available: 950,000 €

Grant amount: up to 50,000 €, covering up to 90% of total project costs.

The remaining 10% must be covered by the applicants as their own contribution in monetary form (not in-kind) and reflected in their accounting statements.

Expected number of grants: 19–25.

Rolling Call — Selection Rounds

This is a rolling call, open for 16 months, with deadlines every three or four months (see indicative timeline). Applications are reviewed and selected after every round deadline.

The rolling structure allows applicants to submit proposals for showcasing projects that are ready to go immediately, as well as those requiring more preparation time — including projects that received co-creation funding through earlier ZMINA:Resilience calls.

Who Can Apply?

Organisations working in the arts and culture sectors, registered in Creative Europe countries (EU countries and non-EU countries).

For Ukraine — registered in territories under the effective control of the Ukrainian government.

While proposals are submitted by a single lead applicant, the project must include at least two partner organisations from at least two countries, one of which is Ukraine. All partners have equal rights and joint responsibility for the correctness of data submitted on the platform and in future reporting.

The partnership must reflect genuine balance and exchange — not a formality. Each partner should play an equally important role, bring equal value, and contribute to reaching audiences in all participating countries.

Eligible Activities

  1. All activities necessary for the preparation and delivery of the presentation events, including:
  2. Public presentation events (in Ukraine, hybrid or online formats are accepted due to the security situation)
  3. Preparation, rehearsals, and production activities related to the presentations
  4. Travel for organisational, rehearsal, and presentation purposes

All projects must include at least 3 presentation events in each of at least 2 countries, one of which must be Ukraine. Presentation events cannot take place in the home city or town of any of the applicant organisations

Eligible Costs

  1. All costs necessary for the implementation of the project
  2. Costs of presenting artistic and cultural works in each partner's country
  3. Travel related to organisational, rehearsal, creative, and presentation purposes

All costs must be incurred after the grant agreement is signed and during the implementation period.

Project Duration

The implementation period is up to 7 months. The earliest start of implementation is after signing the grant agreement.

Technical Eligibility Criteria

  1. All required attachments are uploaded in separate files in the formats specified for this call.
  2. All required attachments follow standard templates available for download on the platform.
  3. All required attachments are readable, accessible, and printable.
  4. All project partners meet the eligibility conditions for this call.
  5. The applicant's registration meets the conditions specified for this call.
  6. The application form is complete and contains all requested information.
  7. The application is submitted by the eligible lead applicant.
  8. The subgrant amount requested does not exceed the maximum set for this call.
  9. The total partner contribution meets the co-financing requirements.
  10. The project implementation period is within the limits set for this call.
  11. The project start date meets the conditions specified for this call.

Applications are checked for technical eligibility by the ZMINA:Resilience team. Proposals found admissible and eligible are forwarded to evaluators (2 per application).

Evaluation Criteria

Relevance:

Relevance of the project to the objectives of this call.

Quality:

Quality of the partnership — equal importance of the roles played by each partner.

Extent to which cross-cutting issues (digital dimension, environmental sustainability, inclusion) and barrier-free access to project results are addressed.

Scale of engagement — expected audience size and number of presentation events.

Impact:

Sustainability of the project, including plans for future showcasing and presentations beyond the grant period.

Selection Procedure

Applications are first reviewed for technical eligibility by the ZMINA:Resilience team to confirm compliance with all formal requirements, including eligibility and admissibility criteria.

Proposals that pass this stage are forwarded to two independent experts for evaluation. Evaluators assign scores, after which applications are ranked by average score.

Final selection is made by the Selection Committee, taking into account geographical, sectoral, and thematic diversity within the available call budget.

The application budget is assessed for cost-effectiveness and justification and may be adjusted prior to signing the grant agreement. The final grant amount is determined based on a combination of lump-sum units and actually incurred costs.

Due to the volume of applications received, the ZMINA:Resilience project team will not be able to provide individual justification for selection decisions. All decisions are final.

How to Apply

Via the IZOLYATSIA online platform, no later than 23:59 (Kyiv time) on the last day of the corresponding selection round: https://platform.izolyatsia.org

The application is submitted by ONE representative of the consortium (the lead applicant).

Language of application: English.

Required Documents

The application package includes:

Application form and budget (filled in directly on the platform).

Supporting documents on capacity, eligibility, and admissibility — uploaded in .pdf format separately for each partner:

Scanned copy of the guarantee letter, completed and signed by the head of the organisation (template available for download on the platform).

Registration documents:

For organisations from Creative Europe countries other than Ukraine — national registration documents with an English translation if the original is in another language.

For organisations from Ukraine — a full extract from the Unified State Register of Legal Entities, Individual Entrepreneurs and Public Organisations, dated after the announcement of this call — in the original language.

Current Statute or equivalent document (if required for the legal entity) — all pages:

For organisations from Creative Europe countries other than Ukraine — with an English translation if the original is in another language.

For organisations from Ukraine — in the original language.

Note: The application form, the budget, the guarantee letter, other supporting documents, and any information the applicant provides to ZMINA:Resilience team are not the mere formality. Where those or any parts thereof are untrue, factually inaccurate, misleading, unfounded, misrepresent the facts, lack factual basis, and the like, providing support to the projects can be terminated at any stage of their lifecycle.

results.content: ZMINA:Resilience. Second call for co-creation funding of international cooperation projects

beneficiaryAdministration:
The IZOLYATSIA Foundation (UA) and Malý Berlín (SK), together with Trans Europe Halles (SE), announce the second call for proposals for the co-creation funding of international cooperation projects.

The objective of the call is to support co-creation between Ukrainian artists and cultural organisations and their peers from Creative Europe countries on the topic of resilience.

Funding will be available for co-creation projects involving at least one Ukrainian partner and a partner from another Creative Europe participating country. Each partner is expected to play a role of comparable weight in the project — whether through creative input, management responsibilities, or audience development. All creative sectors are eligible, with the exception of the audio-visual sector. Each co-creation project must include a public presentation in the locality of every participating partner.

Purpose of the call:

  1. To develop and present an international co-creation on the topic of resilience, in any artistic/cultural sector except audio-visual.
  2. To carry out at least two local presentations (one/locality, including in Ukraine)

Budget:

— Total funding available 187,500€

— Amounts per grant: Up to 25,000€, covering up to 90% of project costs.

— Applicants are expected and required to provide the rest of the total project budget as a contribution.

— Expected number of grants 7-10

Eligible applicants:

Organisations active in the field of arts and culture established in a Creative Europe country (EU countries, non-EU countries). For Ukraine, they must be registered in a zone effectively controlled by the Ukrainian government. Projects must include at least two partners from at least two countries, of which one is Ukraine. Individual artists and freelancers cannot apply directly; they must take part through an eligible organisation acting as a project partner.

List of activities that are eligible for financial support:

— All activities necessary for the co-creation project implementation and development.

— Presentation of the co-creation in the locality of each project partner.

— Travel related to organisational, rehearsal, artistic, presentation purposes.

Duration of the project:

— project duration period: up to 7 months within the indicative implementation window of February–August 2027;

— earliest start of the project after the signature of the grant agreement.

Technical eligibility criteria:

  1. all required attachments (as described in the Application Procedure below) are uploaded to the platform in separate files and in the formats specified for this call;
  2. all required attachments are uploaded to the platform following standard templates that can be downloaded on the platform;
  3. all required attachments are readable, accessible, and printable;
  4. all the project partners meet the eligibility conditions specified for this call;
  5. the registration of all the project partners meets the conditions specified for this call;
  6. the application form is complete and contains all the requested information;
  7. the total subgrant amount requested in the budget is within the maximum subgrant amounts determined for this call;
  8. the total project partners contribution meets the conditions specified for this call;
  9. project implementation period is within the project implementation period defined for this call;
  10. the start of project implementation meets the conditions specified for this call.

Selection criteria:

Relevance:

— relevance of the project to the objectives of the call;

— relevance of potential co-creation to act as a basis for intercultural dialogue.

Quality:

— quality of extent to which cross-cutting issues (digital, green, inclusion) are addressed, including barrier-free access to project results;

— quality of the partnership: the equal importance of the roles played by project partners;

— quality of scale of engagement, measured by the expected audience size and number of local presentations.

Impact:

— Impact and the sustainability of the project, including plans and possibilities for future presentations of the co-creation.

Selection procedure:

Applications will first undergo a technical eligibility check by the ZMINA:Resilience team to verify that they meet all formal requirements, including admissibility and eligibility criteria. Proposals that pass this stage will then be assigned to two independent evaluators each.

Evaluators will assign scores to applications. Then, the applications will be rated according to the average score.

The final selection will be made by the Selection Committee, taking into account geographical, sectoral, and thematic diversity, within the available budget of the call.

The application budget will be assessed for cost-effectiveness and plausibility, and may be adjusted before the grant agreement is signed. The final grant amount will be determined based on a combination of lump sum units and actual costs incurred: costs such as artist fees, travel, accommodation, and per diems are paid at the fixed unit rates listed under "Eligible costs covered by the grant" below, regardless of the exact amount spent, while costs such as equipment rental, production services, and shipping are reimbursed based on actual costs incurred.

Due to the volume of applications received, the ZMINA:Resilience project team will not be able to provide individual feedback for selection decisions. All decisions are final.

Application Procedure

— Applications must be submitted via the IZOLYATSIA online platform no later than 04.12.2026, 23:59 Kyiv time / 22:49 Central European Time on https://platform.izolyatsia.org/en/contest/zmina-resilience-cocreation-two .

— Applicant: The application shall be submitted by a single representative of the consortium/project partners (Lead Applicant).

Required Documents:

  1. The application form and budget (completed directly on the platform),
  2. Supporting documents regarding capacity, eligibility, and admissibility. The following must be uploaded to the platform in .pdf format separately for each partner:
  3. A scanned copy of the Letter of Guarantee, completed and signed by the head of the applicant organization (template available for download on the platform);
  4. Registration documents for organisation registered in Creative Europe countries other than Ukraine: national registration documents with English translation in case the document is issued in another language.
  5. Registration documents for organisation from Ukraine: Full Extract from the Unified State Register of Legal Entities, Physical Persons-Entrepreneurs, and Public Formations dated on or after 5 October 2026 - in their original language.
  6. The current version of the Statutes or equivalent (if mandatory for the legal entity) – all pages: for organisation registered in Creative Europe countries other than Ukraine: with English translation in case the document is issued in another language, for organisation from Ukraine: in their original language.
  7. Language of application: The application must be submitted in English.
  8. Support: During the application period, assistance will be provided through Q&A sessions and a dedicated email helpline.
  9. Subgrant Agreement Template

Funding Conditions

— Financial support: 70% is disbursed upon signing the grant agreement, and the remaining amount is paid upon submission and approval of the report.

— Co-financing is mandatory and must be at least 10% of the total project budget.

— Double funding within the EU budget is not allowed.

— All costs must be incurred after the grant agreement is signed and within the project implementation period.

— Compliance with EU branding and visibility requirements is mandatory.

Eligible costs covered by the grant include

  1. Daily fee for artistic work: 75€/artist/day
  2. Travel: International: 350€/return trip or Local (e.g. participation in trainings): 65€/return trip
  3. Support to green travel (in addition to the travel rate above, for one-way trips over 600km not made by air): 300€ 
  4. Accommodation & per diem: 75€/overnight 
  5. Visa cost, if needed: 80€ 
  6. Shipping/Transport (of equipment), incl. insurance: at cost;
  7. Supplies & equipment (for equipment depreciation costs only): at cost;
  8. Services required for project implementation (production, rental of equipment, rental of space for project events, etc.): at cost;
  9. Communication, marketing and documentation: at cost.
  10. Management and administration costs: Max. 20% of the overall project budget (grant amount plus own contribution/co-financing combined).

Estimated dates:

— Launch of the Call for Proposals: 5 October 2026

— Deadline for Submission of Applications: until 23:59 4December 2026 (Kyiv time)

— Evaluation Period: December 2026

— Announcement of Results: January 2027

— Signing of Grant Agreements: February 2027

— Implementation of Selected Projects: February 2027 – August 2027 (each project runs up to 7 months within this window, depending on its grant agreement signing date)

title: European slate development
descriptionByte:
Scope:

The objective of the European slate development support is to foster the competitiveness of European independent production companies and to increase their economic weight on the market. The aim is also to increase the capacity of audiovisual producers to develop projects with the potential to circulate throughout Europe and beyond, and to facilitate European and international coproduction.

The support will also provide an entry point for emerging talent, giving them the opportunity to direct a short film supported by the strong foundation provided by experienced companies.

Expected results

  • A stronger position on European and international markets for companies selected under European slate development.
  • Increased quality, feasibility, cross-border potential and market value of European works supported.

Description of the activities to be funded

Support will be given to independent European production companies able to develop a slate of 3 to 5 audiovisual works (fiction, animation, creative documentary). This should allow production companies to reduce risks and increase their capacity to attract and retain talents.

The European slate development shall provide support to the development of minimum 3 and maximum 5 works for commercial exploitation intended for cinema release, television broadcasting or commercial exploitation on digital platforms or a multi-platform environment in the following categories: animation, creative documentary or fiction. Applicants may add a short film by emerging talent to their slate (optional).

The aim is to provide funds to audiovisual production companies to develop work with high creative value and cultural diversity and wide cross-border exploitation potential. Companies are encouraged to develop strategies for marketing and distribution from the outset of the development phase thus improving the potential to reach audiences at a European and international level.

Greater cooperation, including co-development, between operators from different countries participating in the MEDIA Strand is also pursued as well as strengthening the competitiveness of European audiovisual production companies by consolidating their capacity for investment in the development phase and expanding companies’ activities and their innovation capacity to explore new fields and markets.

Special attention will be given to applications presenting adequate strategies to ensure a more sustainable and more environmentally-respectful industry and to ensure gender balance, inclusion, diversity and representativeness.

descriptionByte:
Objective:

Expected results:

- Improvement in the trans-national distribution of recent non-national European films.

- Increase in the investment in the production, acquisition, promotion, theatrical and online distribution of non-national European films.

- Develop links between the production and distribution sector thus improving the competitive position of non-national European films.

There are two phases for the funded activities:

1. The generation of a potential fund which will be attributed according to the performance of the company on the European market.

2. The implementation of the action - the potential fund thus generated by each company must be reinvested in:

- the co-production of eligible non-national European films;

- the acquisition of distribution rights, for example by means of minimum guarantees, of eligible non-national European films;

- promotion, marketing and advertising on the market of eligible non-national European films both for theatrical and online releases.

results.summary: AI4CI - Fee waivers for Ulm University
results.content: AI4CI - Fee waivers for Ulm University

beneficiaryAdministration:
1. Aim, Project, Background and Objective

The AI4CI project, co-funded by the European Union under Grant Agreement No. 101123524, provides financial support to students enrolled in the continuing education master’s programme “Artificial Intelligence for Connected Industries” at Ulm University (UUlm), Germany.

The objective of this call is to increase accessibility to advanced digital skills education, support up- and reskilling of professionals, and promote diversity and inclusion in computer science education.

Within this call, up to 80 fee waivers (with a total amount of max. 80.000 EUR), for individual modules in winter term 2026-2027 (October 2026-March 2027) will be awarded.

A fee waiver covers 80 % of the tuition fee of a module in the AI4CI programme. The module fees range from 585 to 1800 Euros. depending on module size in ECTS and specific characteristics of modules (e.g. inclusion of lab times or high amount of tutoring). Fee waivers therefore range between 468 and 1440 Euros.

Fee waivers apply only to modules taken in the semester for which the waiver is granted.

Applicants may apply for fee waivers for multiple modules, provided they are enrolled in these modules.

2. Eligibility

Applicants must fulfil all the following criteria:

1.   Be a citizen of an EU Member State, an EEA country, or a country associated with the Digital Europe Programme (https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/docs/2021-2027/digital/guidance/list-3rd-country-participation_digital_en.pdf),

2.     Be admitted and enrolled in the master’s programme Artificial Intelligence for Connected Industries at Ulm University.

3.     Be registered as a student of the programme in winter semester 2026/2027.

4.     Apply only for modules that

a.  are part of the AI4CI curriculum and

b.     can still be credited toward the final grade and degree.

5.     A fee waiver may be granted only once per module per student.

3. Scope of the Support

  1.       A maximum of 80 module fee waivers will be awarded in this call.
  2.       Each fee waiver reduces the tuition fee of the respective module by 80 %.
  3.       Fee waivers apply only to the semester in which the module is taken.

Students may receive multiple fee waivers, provided they apply for different modules and ranking positions allow it.

4. Application Procedure

4.1 Call Announcement

By 1 October, all admitted students will receive information about:

  1.       the availability of fee waivers,
  2.       the eligibility requirements,
  3.       the application procedure,
  4.       and the application deadline.

4.2 Application Deadline

Applications must be submitted by 1 December 2026.

Applicants must submit:

  1.       a completed application form indicating
  2. other modules they will attend in winter semester 2026-2027, and
  3. other modules for which a fee waiver is requested.
  4.       proof of nationality.
  5.       consent allowing the programme administration to access relevant student data in the HIS student administration system and the App4Master admission system.

Applicants may additionally submit supporting documentation relevant to diversity criteria described in Section 7.

5. Evaluation Procedure

Applications will be evaluated by the Study Programme Committee of the AI4CI programme at Ulm University and the corresponding talent scouting team.

The evaluation will take place within 10 working days after the application deadline.

Each module application is evaluated independently.

Applications will be ranked according to the evaluation criteria defined in Section 6 and the tie-breaking and diversity considerations criteria in section 7.

The highest-ranked module applications will receive a fee waiver.

All remaining eligible applications will be placed on a reserve list.

Applicants will be informed about the outcome within five working days after the evaluation.

6. Evaluation Criteria

The fee waiver scheme supports up- and reskilling in advanced AI competencies.

Applications are evaluated based on the curriculum category of the module.

Points are assigned as follows:

Module Area

Points

A2 Mandatory Area – Artificial Intelligence

3

B1 Systems and Networks

2

B2 Automatics and Robotics

2

B3 Processes and Data Management

2

B4 Free Elective Module

1

All module areas are defined in the Subject-Specific Study and Examination Regulations of the AI4CI programme (10 June 2025) and its additional documents.

The maximum score per module application is 3 points.

7. Tie-Breaking and Diversity Considerations

If multiple applications receive the same score, the following criteria will be applied sequentially to determine priority:

  1. Women and gender minorities
  2. Applicants with disabilities
  3. Applicants with family responsibilities or caregiving duties

Supporting documentation may be provided during the application process.

If applications remain tied after applying the above criteria, the final ranking will be determined by random draw conducted by the study programme committee and the talent scouting team.

8. Award and Implementation of the Fee Waiver

Students selected for a fee waiver will receive an updated tuition fee notice reflecting the 80 % reduction for the respective module.

Receiving a fee waiver does not prevent students from applying for other scholarships, unless the conditions of those programmes prohibit it.

However, double funding from EU sources for the same purpose is not permitted.

If a student receives additional funding, the student must provide a written declaration confirming the absence of EU double funding.

If double funding is identified, the fee waiver may be reduced or withdrawn.

9. Appeals

Applicants may submit an appeal only in cases of procedural errors or factual inaccuracies in the evaluation.

Appeals must:

  1. be submitted in writing within five working days after notification of the results;
  2. clearly indicate the alleged procedural error or incorrect data.

The study programme committee will review the appeal and provide a decision within 10 working days.

10. Termination of the Fee Waiver

The fee waiver may be withdrawn if the student:

  1. withdraws from the programme,
  2. takes academic leave,
  3. transfers to another study programme,
  4. or violates academic integrity or ethical standards.

Students may voluntarily withdraw from the fee waiver by submitting a written request.

Unused funding may be reallocated in a future fee waiver call within the AI4CI project.

11. Publication of Results

The final list of fee waiver recipients will be published no later than 15 December 2026.

Personal data will be processed and published in accordance with applicable data protection regulations.

European Joint Master’s Programme in Digital Society, Social Innovation and Global Citizenship (DIGISOC)
DIGISOC Scholarship Programme Academic Year 2026/2027 UPOL Call for Application

beneficiaryAdministration:
Article 2

Eligibility Criteria


Students enrolled in DIGISOC are eligible to apply for a scholarship only if they meet all of the following criteria:


1.  DIGISOC Students with EU Citizenship or Citizenship from one of the DEP Associates Countries

2.  Students who are enrolled in the second year of the DIGISOC programme for academic year 2026/2027.

3.  DIGISOC Students who have received at least 60 credits for DIGISOC programme courses and completed all courses in which they were enrolled.



Article 3

Application process and period for the academic year 2026/2027


The deadline to submit the applications for the DIGISOC scholarship is 14th December 2026 at 23.59 pm (CET – Central Europe Time).

Applicants are required to upload the necessary documents as listed below on the DIGISOC OpenOlat platform at the following link: 


https://lms.uibk.ac.at/auth/RepositoryEntry/5831590270/CourseNode/113899331829124


Applicants are required to upload the following materials in a single folder labeled with the applicant name:

1)    The signed Application Letter (Annex 1);

2)    The matriculation number at the University which is issuing this call;

3)    The supporting documentation for all eligibility criteria.

The application must be in English. Supporting documents may be submitted in English, Italian, German, or Czech; all other languages require certified translations. If the documentation is not sufficient, the Evaluation Committee mayrequest additional information or reject the application.


Article 4

Evaluation Committee

A joint Evaluation Committee, appointed by the Dean of the Faculty of Law of the Palacký University, reviews all applications and consists of:

·       One representative from each of the three DIGISOC degree awarding universities;

·       At least one DIGISOC student representative;

The Committee is appointed after the deadline for the application submission and terminates the evaluation process no later than 15 days after the deadline.


Article 5

Awarding Criteria and Evaluation Procedure


The joint Evaluation Committee will check eligibility criteria and evaluate each application.

The candidate academic excellence will be evaluated based on the weighted average of grades achieved during academic year 2025/2026 in all DIGISOC courses, calculated and rounded to hundredths (e.g. 28,77) on a 30 points scale according to the DIGISOC grade conversion table. Based on averages, students who have submitted their application will be put in descending order. In case of tie, they will be put on shared place, awarding the higher award.


To determine the exact amount of the scholarship allocated to each applicant, the joint Evaluation Committee will use the following model:


·      the Student with highest average will be awarded a 2000 EUR scholarship.

·      the Student with second highest average will be awarded a 1750 EUR scholarship.

·      the Student with third highest average will receive a 1500 EUR scholarship.

·      All other students with average above 26,99 will receive a scholarship which corresponds to the result of dividing the call's remaining budget by the number of applications fulfilling the award criteria, but not exceeding 1000 EUR per applicant.


The joint Evaluation Committee’s judgement is unquestionable.

The rankings and the exact amount of funding received by each applicant will be published on the DIGISOC website (https://digitalsociety4innovation.eu/costs-and-scholarships/) and the DIGISOC Awarding Universities Websites. This publication has the value of notification.
description:
Article 1

Purpose, amount and duration of the DIGISOC Scholarship


The Palacký University is issuing a Call for Application within the DIGISOC Scholarship Programme, reserved for students enrolled for the Academic Year 2026/2027 in the second year of the Joint Master’s Programme in Digital Society, Social Innovation and Global Citizenship (DIGISOC).

The Call for Application has a total budget of EUR 11.000,00.

The DIGISOC Scolarship Programme is designed to provide financial support to students participating in the DIGISOC Joint Master’s Programme (JMP) and aims to:

·      Reward students with outstanding academic performance;

·      Promote excellence in higher education;

·      Alleviate costs associated with tuition fees, summer schools, short-term mobilities, and living expenses.

The scholarships also function as a form of social support, helping students overcome personal or socio-economic obstacles that hinder participation in international education.

The DIGISOC scholarship is limited to one academic year. The scholarships are paid out in one instalment.

There is no automatic entitlement to scholarships and there is no automatic renewal.

The application must be in English. Supporting documents may be submitted in English, Italian, German, or Czech; all other languages require certified translations. If the documentation is not sufficient, the Evaluation Committee mayrequest additional information or reject the application.

Awarding Criteria and Evaluation Procedure


The joint Evaluation Committee will check eligibility criteria and evaluate each application.

The candidate academic excellence will be evaluated based on the weighted average of grades achieved during academic year 2025/2026 in all DIGISOC courses, calculated and rounded to hundredths (e.g. 28,77) on a 30 points scale according to the DIGISOC grade conversion table. To determine the exact amount of the scholarship allocated to each applicant, the joint Evaluation Committee will use the following model:


·      the Student with highest average will be awarded a 2000 EUR scholarship.

·      the Student with second highest average will be awarded a 1750 EUR scholarship.

·      the Student with third highest average will receive a 1500 EUR scholarship.

·      All other students with average above 26,99 will receive a scholarship which corresponds to the result of dividing the call's remaining budget by the number of applications fulfilling the award criteria, but not exceeding 1000 EUR per applicant.

Eligibility Criteria

Students enrolled in DIGISOC for the second year are eligible to apply for a scholarship if they meet one or more of the following criteria:

1. Students with certified disabilities

Students with certified disabilities can apply for a DIGISOC scholarship. In the context of this call, and following Article 1 of the European Disability Policy, students with disabilities are considered students who have long-term physical, mental, intellectual or sensory impairments which, in interaction with various barriers, may hinder their full and effective participation in society on an equal basis with others. Applicants must provide certified medical documentation or proof of a national disability status.

2. Migrants or refugees

Students who are migrants or refugees can apply for funding based on their status. Required proof may include an asylum decision, a residence permit, or confirmation issued by a migration authority.

3. Students with low socio-economic family conditions

Students from families with low socio-economic conditions can apply for funding. Low socio-economic conditions are defined according to the student’s family income. Required proof may include a tax statement, an income certificate, or an official social benefit statement.

4. Students living in remote areas

Students living in a region in the lowest 25% of national population density and/or with no regular access to higher education within a 100 km radius may apply. Required proof is a residence certificate, which will be assessed against infrastructure data based on national statistics.


Application process and period for the academic year 2026/2027

The deadline to submit applications for the DIGISOC scholarships is 10. December 2026 at 23.59 CET (Central European Time).

Applicants are required to upload the necessary documents listed below on the DIGISOC OpenOlat platform at the following link:

https://lms.uibk.ac.at/auth/RepositoryEntry/5831590270/CourseNode/114518610654144

Applicants are required to upload the following materials in a single folder labelled with the applicant’s name:

·       The signed Application Letter (Annex 1);

·       The applicant’s registration number (Matrikelnummer) at the University of Innsbruck;

·       The supporting documentation for each claimed eligibility criterion, issued by a responsible authority or accredited expert.

·       The Data Protection and Consent Declaration (Annex 2).

The application must be in English. Supporting documents may be submitted in English, Italian, German, or Czech; documents in other languages require certified translations. If the documentation is insufficient, the Evaluation Committee may request additional information or reject the application.

By submitting the application and signing Annex 1, the applicant expressly confirms that the application has been submitted completely and correctly and that all information and supporting documents are accurate and complete. Incomplete applications may be excluded from the selection procedure.


Evaluation Committee

A joint Evaluation Committee, appointed by the Study Coordinator (Studienbeauftragter) of the Faculty of Economics and Statistics of the University of Innsbruck, reviews all applications and consists of:

·       One representative from each of the three DIGISOC degree-awarding universities;

·       At least one student representative from the University of Innsbruck;

·       Disability officer at the University of Innsbruck.

The Committee is appointed after the deadline for application submission and completes the evaluation process no later than 15 days after the deadline.


Awarding Criteria and Evaluation Procedure

The joint Evaluation Committee will evaluate each application and award points based on the following criteria:

1. Students with certified disabilities

Applicants will be awarded points on the basis of the severity and impact of their condition, ranging from 5 points for a comparatively less impactful disability to 10 points for a very serious disability.

2. Migrants or refugees

Applicants will be awarded points as follows: 

a.         10 points for refugee status; 

b.         10 points for migrant status with less than 5 years in the current country of residence; 

c.         5 points for migrant status with 5 or more years in the current country of residence.

3. Low socio-economic family condition

Applicants will be awarded 10 points if their family income falls within the first quartile (Q1), i.e. within the 25% of the population with the lowest incomes in their country of origin. Applicants will be awarded 5 points if their family income falls between the first and second quartile (Q2), i.e. within the range defined by the median income and Q1 in their country of origin. The reference fiscal year is the year preceding the year in which the application is submitted.

4. Remote areas

Applicants will be awarded 5 points for residence in a remote area. An additional 5 points will be awarded if the student’s residence is in a remote area with no regular access to higher education within a 100 km radius.

All applications will be ranked on the basis of the sum of points obtained across the four criteria. Each application can obtain a maximum of 30 points.

To determine the exact amount of the scholarship allocated to each applicant, the joint Evaluation Committee will use a proportional point-based model:

·       Total funds available are divided by the sum of all points awarded across valid applications;

·       This determines a value per point (EUR/point);

·       Each applicant receives funding according to their own score, up to the maximum of EUR 3,000.00.

The decision of the joint Evaluation Committee is final, subject to the appeal procedure set out in Article 6.

The exact amount of funding and its composition awarded to each applicant will be published via the Learning Management System OpenOLAT. This publication constitutes as notification.
description:
Purpose, amount and duration of the DIGISOC Scholarship

The University of Innsbruck is issuing a Call for Application within the DIGISOC Scholarship Programme, reserved for students enrolled for the Academic Year 2026/2027 in the second year of the Joint Master’s Programme in Digital Society, Social Innovation and Global Citizenship (DIGISOC).

The Call for Application has a total budget of EUR 50.000.

The DIGISOC Scholarship Programme is designed to provide financial support to students participating in the DIGISOC Joint Master’s Programme (JMP) and aims to:

·       Alleviate costs associated with tuition fees, summer schools, short-term mobilities, and living expenses;

·       Support students from underprivileged or vulnerable backgrounds;

·       Promote diversity, fairness, and gender balance in higher education.

The scholarship also functions as a form of social support, helping students overcome personal or socio-economic obstacles that hinder participation in international education.

The DIGISOC Scholarship is limited to one academic year and is paid out in one instalment. There is no automatic entitlement to a scholarship and no automatic renewal.

The amount of the scholarship can reach a maximum of EUR 3,000.00 gross per academic year and applicant. The exact amount assigned to each applicant is based on the points awarded in the evaluation process (see Article 5 – Awarding Criteria and Evaluation Procedure).

A maximum of 30 points can be awarded to each application. The maximum total funding per student is EUR 6,000.00 over the course of the two-year programme.

For the entire academic year for which the scholarship is awarded, the scholarship holder must not have an employment relationship with the University of Innsbruck. 

Applicants and scholarship holders are solely responsible for clarifying and complying with all tax obligations and any other individual tax consequences arising from receipt of the scholarship. The University of Innsbruck does not provide individual tax advice.

With the declaration of acceptance, the scholarship holder must also undertake to communicate any change occurring during the academic year that affects information previously declared or eligibility for the scholarship.


Requirements for receiving the scholarship

Before disbursement, the scholarship holder will complete the required scholarship documentation with the University of Innsbruck and must provide:

·       A current enrolment certificate showing the register number;

·       The applicant’s full residential address (street and house number, postal code, city, and country);

·       Bank details for an account held in the scholarship holder’s name, including an IBAN and any further information required to enable a SEPA credit transfer. It must be expressly possible to make the scholarship payment by SEPA transfer to the account provided;

Scholarship holders remain solely responsible for all tax-law clarifications and obligations connected with the scholarship.

The scholarship holder must also confirm that no employment relationship with the University of Innsbruck exists or will exist for the duration of the academic year for which the scholarship is awarded.


Financial and Disbursement Procedures

Scholarships are paid in one instalment per academic year. 

Disbursement is handled by the University of Innsbruck as the DIGISOC degree-awarding university issuing this Call for Application.

The scholarship holder is responsible for providing complete and correct bank details and for any bank charges or conversion costs that may arise outside the scope of the SEPA payment.


Renunciation

In the event of withdrawal from the scholarship after acceptance, scholarship holders must give written notice by e-mail to digisoc@uibk.ac.at.

beneficiaryAdministration:
The Call has 5 distinct cut-off dates. All submitted applications (for the two objectives/priorities) by each deadline will be evaluated jointly and awarded until funding resources are available. The AI4Gov-X consortium reserves the right of integrating the funding budget with an extra allocation, until twice the initially allocated amount.

Applications will be possible electronically and exclusively managed through the GoodGrantsTM platform (https://polidesign.grantplatform.com/) by filling in a form and attaching the required documentation. Beneficiaries must be natural persons and as a precondition, be enrolled students in the MagiX master's course (for objectives/priorities 1 and 2) and/or (for objective/priority 1) in one or more of the AI4Gov-X extracurricular activities, strictly identified from the list published on the project's website, at this link: https://ai4gov-x.eu/extracurricular-activities/. Please note that the list will be updated on a monthly basis while the Call is open. Additionally for objective/priority 2 only, beneficiaries must be unemployed people, able to document the existence of an internship contract with a host organisation from the public or private sector, residing in an eligible country for the Call (for a full list see Further information below).

A same natural person holding the necessary requisites may apply to both objectives within the same cut-off date or within two distinct cut-off dates. However, he or she can receive the financial benefits of either objective/priority only once.

Evaluation of received applications will be done by a special committee established at the Funding Body, POLI.design. Each application will be evaluated from the perspectives of admissibility, eligibility, and merit.

For both priorities/objectives, admissibility conditions will be that an electronic application has been received on or before the latest cut-off date, completed in all its parts, and with all required attachments, exclusively through the GoodGrantsTM platform. Incomplete applications or submitted by other means will be discarded and proposed for resubmission at the next cut-off date.

To pass the admissibility check, all applicants must submit at least:

- A signed application form,

- Their CV in Europass format (see https://europass.europa.eu/en/create-europass-cv),

- A motivation letter, specifically mentioning their employment status,

- Any documentation supporting disadvantaged background and/or priority categories (where applicable),

- Signed declarations (on conflict of interest, double funding, etc.) using the templates available on the GoodGrantsTM platform.

Applicants to priority/objective 1 must additionally submit:

- A proof of enrollment or acceptance in the MagiX master's course and/or in an extracurricular activity of the AI4Gov-X programme, dated not earlier than the opening of this Call and not yet finalised by the chosen cut-off date, and

- An indicative cost breakdown (travel, accommodation, fees, etc.).

Applicants to priority/objective 2 must additionally submit:

- A proof of enrollment or acceptance in the MagiX master's course,

- Copy of an internship contract, or equivalent legally binding agreement, dated not earlier than the opening of this Call and not yet finalised by the chosen cut-off date, showing the amount paid by the host organisation.

All the above documentation must be provided in English language. Unofficial translations are allowed in case of submission of documents that are natively not in English, but the applicant will take the risk and bear the consequences of any misinterpretation during the evaluation process.

For both priorities/objectives, eligibility conditions will be that

- The applicants must be natural persons and nationals of an eligible country for the Call (see Further information below).

- They must be enrolled in, or formally accepted into, the MagiX master's course and/or any of the extracurricular activities of AI4Gov-X (depending on the priority/objective) at the time of application.

- They must not be subject to restrictive measures or other disqualifying conditions according to the EU or national legislation in their country.

- They cannot receive double funding for the same operation.

- They cannot be awarded twice under the same priority/objective.

- They must not be in a situation of conflict of interest with POLI.design or any other AI4Gov-X partner.

For priority/objective 2 only, a supplementary eligibility condition will be that

- The applicants must be unemployed people documenting their enrollment in an internship programme at a host organisation residing in an eligible country (see Further information below).

Eligible applications received until the same cut-off date will be scored using the following criteria (max. 100 points):

Criterion

Description

Score

Excellence and relevance

Academic/professional background and relevance to AI4Gov-X topics

0–30

Motivation and expected impact

Motivation, expected learning and career impact

0–25

Financial need

Economic situation and justification of need

0–25

European added value

Cross-border dimension, diversity contribution, EU public sector fit

0–20

No minimum thresholds or weighting will be applied. In case of equal scores, the following priority rules will be adopted, in the same order:

- Applicants documenting their enrollment in (or acceptance into) both the MagiX master's course and at least one extracurricular activity of the AI4Gov-X programme (only for objective/priority 1);

- Applicants coming from countries that are not full members of the AI4Gov-X consortium.

- Applicants from regions with average income below 75% of the EU average.

as reported in the indicative cost breakdown (see above). The Selection Committee may cap specific cost items if considered excessive or not in line with typical market prices for the location and period.

title: Specialised education programmes in key capacity areas
duration: This Call has two distinct objectives/priorities, each associated with a separate application and evaluation process: 1) To provide financial assistance to deserving students, enrolled in the AI4Gov-X programme's master’s course and/or extracurricular activities, reducing the economic barriers to accessing high-quality education, and 2) To facilitate the creation of employment opportunities for the participants in the AI4Gov-X master's course (aka MagiX).
destinationDetails:
The Call has 5 distinct cut-off dates. All submitted applications (for the two objectives/priorities) by each deadline will be evaluated jointly and awarded until funding resources are available. The AI4Gov-X consortium reserves the right of integrating the funding budget with an extra allocation, until twice the initially allocated amount.

Applications will be possible electronically and exclusively managed through the GoodGrantsTM platform (https://polidesign.grantplatform.com/) by filling in a form and attaching the required documentation. Beneficiaries must be natural persons and as a precondition, be enrolled students in the MagiX master's course (for objectives/priorities 1 and 2) and/or (for objective/priority 1) in one or more of the AI4Gov-X extracurricular activities, strictly identified from the list published on the project's website, at this link: https://ai4gov-x.eu/extracurricular-activities/. Please note that the list will be updated on a monthly basis while the Call is open. Additionally for objective/priority 2 only, beneficiaries must be unemployed people, able to document the existence of an internship contract with a host organisation from the public or private sector, residing in an eligible country for the Call (for a full list see Further information below).

A same natural person holding the necessary requisites may apply to both objectives within the same cut-off date or within two distinct cut-off dates. However, he or she can receive the financial benefits of either objective/priority only once.

Evaluation of received applications will be done by a special committee established at the Funding Body, POLI.design. Each application will be evaluated from the perspectives of admissibility, eligibility, and merit.

For both priorities/objectives, admissibility conditions will be that an electronic application has been received on or before the latest cut-off date, completed in all its parts, and with all required attachments, exclusively through the GoodGrantsTM platform. Incomplete applications or submitted by other means will be discarded and proposed for resubmission at the next cut-off date.

To pass the admissibility check, all applicants must submit at least:

- A signed application form,

- Their CV in Europass format (see https://europass.europa.eu/en/create-europass-cv),

- A motivation letter, specifically mentioning their employment status,

- Any documentation supporting disadvantaged background and/or priority categories (where applicable),

- Signed declarations (on conflict of interest, double funding, etc.) using the templates available on the GoodGrantsTM platform.

Applicants to priority/objective 1 must additionally submit:

- A proof of enrollment or acceptance in the MagiX master's course and/or in an extracurricular activity of the AI4Gov-X programme, dated not earlier than the opening of this Call and not yet finalised by the chosen cut-off date, and

- An indicative cost breakdown (travel, accommodation, fees, etc.).

Applicants to priority/objective 2 must additionally submit:

- A proof of enrollment or acceptance in the MagiX master's course,

- Copy of an internship contract, or equivalent legally binding agreement, dated not earlier than the opening of this Call and not yet finalised by the chosen cut-off date, showing the amount paid by the host organisation.

All the above documentation must be provided in English language. Unofficial translations are allowed in case of submission of documents that are natively not in English, but the applicant will take the risk and bear the consequences of any misinterpretation during the evaluation process.

For both priorities/objectives, eligibility conditions will be that

- The applicants must be natural persons and nationals of an eligible country for the Call (see Further information below).

- They must be enrolled in, or formally accepted into, the MagiX master's course and/or any of the extracurricular activities of AI4Gov-X (depending on the priority/objective) at the time of application.

- They must not be subject to restrictive measures or other disqualifying conditions according to the EU or national legislation in their country.

- They cannot receive double funding for the same operation.

- They cannot be awarded twice under the same priority/objective.

- They must not be in a situation of conflict of interest with POLI.design or any other AI4Gov-X partner.

For priority/objective 2 only, a supplementary eligibility condition will be that

- The applicants must be unemployed people documenting their enrollment in an internship programme at a host organisation residing in an eligible country (see Further information below).

beneficiaryAdministration:
To apply, the following requirements must be met:

  1. The applicant is a company registered in the Estonian Commercial Register.
  2. The company’s business activity is related to cybersecurity products and/or services.
  3. The applicant’s principal activity falls under EMTAK 2025 Division K, including:
  4. Telecommunications
  5. Computer programming
  6. IT consulting
  7. Computing infrastructure and other information service activities
  8. The company’s EMTAK code must be compatible with the scope of the support scheme
  9. The project must involve at least one partner, such as a research or development institution
  10. All project activities must take place within the EU or EEA (EU Member States, Norway, Iceland, or Liechtenstein)
  11. Both the applicant company and the entity controlling the project partner must be registered in the EU or EEA.

To apply, the following steps must be completed:

  1. Identify a suitable research or development partner - Find a research or development institution that matches your project idea
  2. Discuss the project idea with the partner - Agree on the project scope, objectives, expected results, and roles
  3. Request a price quote - Obtain a formal price offer from the research or development institution for their planned work
  4. Prepare the project plan - Describe the project objectives, activities, timeline, budget, and expected impact
  5. Complete the application form - Fill in the required information in the E-grant self-service environment
  6. Submit the application and supporting documents - Upload the project plan, price offer, and all other required documents in E-grant and submit the application.
description: The grant will help strengthen cooperation between research and development institutions and companies or organisations involved in the development of cybersecurity products and services, in order to carry out innovation and development activities in the field of cybersecurity.

furtherInformation:
A company may apply for support in the amount of €60,000 to €100,000 of the total cost of the product development project. The grant amounts to 70% of the total project costs for micro and small enterprises, 60% for medium-sized enterprises, and 50% for large enterprises.

The grant is targeted at projects carrying out innovation and development activities in the following areas:

  1. cybersecurity automation
  2. the use of artificial intelligence in cybersecurity
  3. tools and strategies for the transition to quantum-resistant cryptographic algorithms
  4. cybersecurity of space technologies

The call deadline of 2 December 2026, may be extended depending on the availability of funding.

Further information on the Innovation Funding is provided by RIA (Estonian Information System Authority) and EIS (Estonian Business and Innovation Agency) websites.

descriptionByte:
Expected Outcome:

Projects are expected to contribute to the following expected outcomes:

  • Advanced heterogeneous integration, particularly in 2.5D and 3D packaging and integrated photonics, to support AI functionalities.

  • Standardised chiplet interfaces, enabling interoperability and fostering a dynamic chiplet ecosystem

Expected outcomes should have direct and immediate impact on European industry.

Furthermore, proposed projects should demonstrate solutions across laboratory and pilot environments, with verification in semiconductor manufacturing use cases. The centre of gravity of envisaged work should address Technology Readiness Levels 5-7. Proposals also need to facilitate knowledge transfer and promote stakeholder engagement through industry workshops, publications, and networking events.

description: As part of its activities, FuseNet supports the FuseNet member institutions with the organisation of mini-workshops. These are small-scale workshops that aim to connect young talents with experienced researchers. They have the set-up of masterclasses on a dedicated topic, include interaction between experts and students and are organised for either MSc or PhD students. Such events typically last 2–5 days. This call is for mini-workshops that are to be organised before the end of this year.

results.summary: FuseNet Support of Master Students going on an internship abroad
results.content: FuseNet Support of Master Students going on an internship abroad

beneficiaryAdministration:
The submission of applications is done via the dedicated FuseNet page. The submitted applications are evaluated by the FuseNet Executive Office. Decision to the student is communicated by email, within 2 weeks after complete submission of the application.

Only in case of doubt regarding eligibility, the FuseNet Executive Office consults the Academic Council of FuseNet (in written procedure). The decision of the Academic Council of FuseNet is final and binding and cannot be discussed or changed again.
description:
This support package is meant to facilitate MSc students in fusion who want to go abroad for an internship, thereby stimulating quality of education through exchanges. The internship can take place at a fusion research centre or university involved in fusion research. This place is not limited to Europe. Students registered at universities that are a FuseNet member and/or are doing their internship at hosts that are a FuseNet member, and their home university is located in one of the EUROfusion member states can apply for financial support for their internship here.

The financial support consists of a fixed amount of travel support (depending on the travel distance) and accommodation/living support (depending on the internship duration). The application has to be submitted at least 2 weeks before and within 6 months of the start of the internship. Other sources of funding for the internship (scholarships or grants, compensation or salary from the host institute, funds from other EU support schemes, etc.) need to be specified. Funding can also be restricted in cases where funding has been received from FuseNet in the past (see the terms and conditions on the FuseNet webpage).

results.content: FuseNet Support of Master Students in attending Educational Events

beneficiaryAdministration:
The submission of applications is done via the FuseNet website. The submitted applications are evaluated by the FuseNet Executive Office. Decision to the student will be communicated by email, typically within 2 weeks after complete submission of the application.

Only in case of doubt regarding eligibility, the FuseNet Executive Office consults the Academic Council of FuseNet (in written procedure). The decision of the Academic Council of FuseNet is final and binding and cannot be discussed or changed again.
description:
This support scheme is launched to support and facilitate Master students to take part in educational activities external to their own organization. It allows Master students to participate in fusion Master classes, summer schools, and other short-term events with a dominant educational character. All conferences are excluded from support except when the Master student has his/her own contribution at the event (see terms and conditions for details).

Students registered at universities that are a FuseNet member and/or are seeking to attend educational activities at hosts that are a FuseNet member, and both the home university and the educational event are located in one of the countries that are part of the EUROfusion member states, can apply here for financial support to take part in a fusion-related educational training activity.

The financial support consists of a fixed amount of travel support (depending on the travel distance) and subsistence support (depending on the duration). The (training) activity has to take place at a university group or research institute in one of the EUROfusion members states or at a FuseNet member institute. The application has to be submitted at least 2 weeks before the actual start of the educational event. The educational event has to start no later than 6 months after application.

6. Legal and financial set-up of the grants

Eligible costs will take the form of a lump sum as defined in the Decision of 7 July 2021 authorising the use of lump sum contributions under the Horizon Europe Programme – the Framework Programme for Horizon Europe for Research and Innovation (2021-2027) – and in actions under the Research and Training Programme of the European Atomic Energy Community (2021-2025).

The consortium must provide financial support to third parties (FSTP) for the implementation of this action.
Since providing FSTP is a core activity of this action, the EUR 60 000 threshold laid down in Article 207 of Financial Regulation (EU, Euratom) 2024/2509 does not apply. The maximum amount of FSTP provided in form of grants that may be awarded to any single third party is set at EUR 300 000 for the entire duration of the action. This ceiling is justified by the fact that FSTP is a primary activity of this action, by its expected duration of 1-2 years, including costs of relocation and of a European competitive salary for an internationally mobile expert at PhD level, and by the extensive experience gained by the Enterprise Europe Network in providing business support to SMEs. However, if the objectives of the action would otherwise be impossible or overly difficult the maximum amount may be higher if duly justified in the proposal.

The Consortium must allocate at least 90% of the total proposed budget to FSTP.

title: Skills for innovative SMEs
descriptionByte:
Expected Outcome:

  • Establishment of an SME support scheme through the Enterprise Europe Network, which delivers transnational skills-matching, recruitment support, and innovation management services to innovative SMEs across Europe.
  • This support scheme has the following expected outcomes: Innovative SMEs have reduced labour and skill shortages through a transnational mobility scheme, which allows them to recruit and train highly skilled researchers from abroad;
  • SMEs have improved innovation capacity to support research and innovation (R&I) projects and increased participation of highly skilled staff employed in R&I through recruitment and training;
  • Researchers gain new knowledge and skills in industrial innovation and business management, through employment and training in innovative companies.

Scope:

To facilitate the innovation to investment journey and boost competitiveness, the EU needs to promote skills and quality jobs and help SMEs strengthen their innovation potential, by addressing labour and skills shortages, as highlighted in the Competitiveness Compass for the EU. Europe faces a growing challenge in meeting the demand for skilled talent in strategic sectors like clean and circular technologies, energy, health, biotech, agriculture, bioeconomy, digital technologies, aerospace and civil security. The progressive loss of women in science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) careers, also known as the ‘leaky pipeline’, is further increasing these skills shortages. Nearly four in five SMEs say they cannot find the talent they need. The lack of access to skills, including the latest scientific knowledge and capacity to manage innovation processes effectively, have been identified as major barriers for innovation in SMEs, especially among start-ups and scale-ups.

In line with the 'Choose Europe for Science' initiative, this action is expected to set up a transnational mobility scheme to provide lump sum grants (via FSTP) to innovative SMEs who have experienced skill shortages and difficulty in recruiting innovation talent.

The action builds on the successful results of the ‘European SME innovation associate pilot’, which was launched in three consecutive calls under the Horizon 2020 work programmes 2016 – 2020. An evaluation study[1] of this pilot found that the grant was instrumental for most SMEs to recruit an innovation associate and that most supported SMEs were able to bring the results of their innovation projects to market. The insights from this earlier action should be reflected in any proposal. The action also complements Marie Skłodowska Curie Actions (MSCA), by providing additional work opportunities for researchers/early-career professionals holding a PhD, including but not limited to those who completed the MSCA fellowship, and aim to gain further experience in the private sector. Existing structures, such as the European Universities alliances, may offer SMEs further access to trainings, resources, networks, facilities and infrastructures across Europe.

The selected consortium shall organise and manage the SME support scheme. In particular, the consortium is expected to:

  • Ensure the sound design and implementation of the SME support scheme, including launching the call, eligibility checks, evaluations, and business support, where necessary.
  • Promote the scheme to secure quality applications, monitor impact (including on skills development) and disseminate success stories of the innovation-to-investment journey.
  • Provide support to funded SMEs for the transnational recruitment of researchers, including through the EURAXESS network and assistance with visa applications;
  • Organise networking events and training on industrial innovation and business management, and promote cooperation among the community of researchers and funded SMEs;
  • Ensure equal access across EU Member States and Horizon Europe Associated Countries and balanced distribution of strategic sectors.

Eligible third parties to the FSTP scheme are SMEs that have an innovation idea and can demonstrate that the relevant skills cannot be found on the national labour market (e.g. by providing data on labour and skills shortages on the national context). SMEs should include in their application to an FSTP call a description of their innovation idea, a vacancy notice specifying the knowledge and skills needed for the development of the project, and a recruitment plan, which offers equal opportunities to researchers of all genders. Upon successful evaluation organised by the consortium, selected SMEs are expected to advertise their vacancy on the EURAXESS portal and other relevant platforms, with clear indication that the grant was awarded, in order to recruit the researchers.

The scheme encourages transnational mobility of PhD knowledge holders, including MSCA fellows who have completed their fellowships at the date of recruitment. In the case of MSCA fellows, since they have already met the MSCA mobility rule, they do not need to move again if selected by an SME in their current country of residence. Additionally, SMEs may hire researchers with the nationality of the country in which the SME is located, as long as those researchers are currently employed and residing abroad.

Moreover, the scheme should be open to recruit researchers both from STEM disciplines and social sciences and humanities (SSH) background, who could bring social innovation practices or an interdisciplinary perspective to the innovation capacity of the SMEs.

These essential specificities are expected to be built into the SME support scheme:

  • Competitive salary of the researcher / total employers’ costs including full social security according to national legislation for the researcher for a minimum duration of 12 months and a maximum duration of 24 months (including the salaries actually paid if the researcher leaves before 12 months).
  • Relocation costs of the researcher, which may include removal cost, travel cost of the researcher and their immediate family (if applicable) to the new place of employment, visa cost (if applicable), translation cost of certificates (if applicable), a temporary transition allowance to cover extra costs upon arrival in the place of employment, cost for the relocation in the country of origin after the project (if applicable), a family and childcare allowance (if applicable), as well as other clearly justified expenditure directly related to relocation.
  • Travel to conferences and workshops, as well as access to and use of technological and research infrastructures, or other activities relevant to the SME’s innovation idea.

[1] European Commission: Executive Agency for Small and Medium-sized Enterprises, Ramboll, LE Europe, DIW, CARSA, ECORYS, Botnari, A., Hahn, F., Juskevicius, R., Lübbers, T., Muller, P., Riviere, M., Savickaite, I., Sierra, N.Weström, P., Accompanying study to the European SME Innovation Associate – Pilot action – Final report, Publications Office, 2019, https://data.europa.eu/doi/10.2826/645018

supportInfo:
Online Manual is your guide on the procedures from proposal submission to managing your grant.

Horizon Europe Programme Guide contains the detailed guidance to the structure, budget and political priorities of Horizon Europe.

Funding & Tenders Portal FAQ – find the answers to most frequently asked questions on submission of proposals, evaluation and grant management.

Research Enquiry Service – ask questions about any aspect of European research in general and the EU Research Framework Programmes in particular.

National Contact Points (NCPs) – get guidance, practical information and assistance on participation in Horizon Europe. There are also NCPs in many non-EU and non-associated countries (‘third-countries’).

Enterprise Europe Network – contact your EEN national contact for advice to businesses with special focus on SMEs. The support includes guidance on the EU research funding.

IT Helpdesk – contact the Funding & Tenders Portal IT helpdesk for questions such as forgotten passwords, access rights and roles, technical aspects of submission of proposals, etc.

European IPR Helpdesk assists you on intellectual property issues.

CEN-CENELEC Research Helpdesk and ETSI Research Helpdesk – the European Standards Organisations advise you how to tackle standardisation in your project proposal.
